newsitem.title: USA: Petitions submitted to force Miami arena vote.
newsitem.headline: Petitions submitted to force Miami arena vote.

text.p: A Miami attorney submitted petitions signed by voters seeking to force a referendum on the use of tax money to build a new $165 million basketball arena for the Miami Heat.
Attorney Dan Paul said the petitions had 48,672 voter signatures, far more than the 30,577 needed to put the arena question on the Nov 5 ballot.
Paul submitted the petitions Thursday for signature verification. Dade County Elections Supervisor David Leahy said the results would be known early next week.

Under a plan approved by the county commission, the Miami Sports and Exhibition Authority will issue revenue bonds to build the arena on public waterfront land near the Port of Miami. The team will contribute $50 million, and the rest of the debt service would be paid from arena revenues, hotel bed taxes and a sales tax rebate.
The bonds would carry a backup pledge from county operating revenues.
Paul objected to the financing plan and the arena site.
A poll by the Miami Herald said 60 percent of respondents opposed the arena project, but Heat officials said their polling shows overwhelming support for it.
